chunks.title: Professional summary
chunks.text: Mahmoud Alyosify is an AI & Machine Learning Engineer who builds end-to-end intelligent systems across LLM fine-tuning and inference optimisation, multi-agent systems, self-supervised learning, and reinforcement learning. He is completing an MSc in Artificial Intelligence at Queen's University, Canada on a Digilians Presidential Scholarship, with a master's research project on training-free, decoding-time efficiency for large language models. He has delivered production-oriented systems on AWS spanning autonomous OSINT threat intelligence, retrieval-ready vision pipelines, deep-RL cloud autoscaling, and satellite collision risk prediction. He has taught over 10,000 learners with more than 700,000 YouTube views. He is seeking AI/ML engineering roles in LLM systems, MLOps, and efficient inference at scale.

chunks.title: Depth of AI expertise
chunks.text: Mahmoud's deepest AI expertise is in four areas. First, LLM systems: fine-tuning open-weight models (LoRA/QLoRA/PEFT), custom decoding strategies implemented as LogitsProcessors, and rigorous inference benchmarking. Second, multi-agent and agentic systems: swarms of specialised agents that collect and correlate information into knowledge graphs, and agentic workflows that chain extraction, generation and synthesis. Third, self-supervised and contrastive representation learning for vision, including SimCLR and SupCon with ONNX/FAISS retrieval deployment. Fourth, deep reinforcement learning applied to systems problems, notably PPO and DQN for cloud resource provisioning. He also does applied RAG, generative AI, and cloud AI deployment on AWS.

chunks.title: Verbosity-Aware Decoding for Token-Efficient Language Model Inference
chunks.text: Verbosity-Aware Decoding for Token-Efficient Language Model Inference — Mahmoud's MSc research project (CISC 898) at Queen's University, supervised by Dr. Rahatara Ferdousi, July 2026 to present. He designed a training-free LogitsProcessor that cuts generated tokens at decoding time by combining stop-token, n-gram-repetition and semantic-redundancy signals under an entropy-driven gate — with no retraining, no architecture change, and no KV-cache or attention overhead. Validated across three open-weight model families (Mistral-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct) on MT-Bench, YapBench, XSum and SQuAD-v2. He built a pre-registered evaluation protocol proving semantic preservation through paired non-inferiority testing (BERTScore, ROUGE, exact-match/F1, length-controlled LLM judge) alongside token reduction, latency (time-to-first-token and inter-token), and GPU energy measured via NVML — fully deterministic and reproducible on pinned AWS GPU instances. Repository: https://github.com/MahmoudAlyosify/minimal-lm

chunks.title: HORUS Sentinel — Autonomous Multi-Agent OSINT & Threat-Intelligence Platform
chunks.text: HORUS Sentinel is an autonomous multi-agent OSINT and threat-intelligence platform, built May 2026 to July 2026 in Python. Mahmoud architected an autonomous intelligence analyst in which a swarm of specialised passive agents continuously collects open-source intelligence and correlates every finding into a living Intelligence Knowledge Graph. A self-hosted, fine-tuned language model reasons over the graph to deliver prioritised, evidence-backed intelligence reports, compressing hours of manual analyst work into minutes. Repository: https://github.com/MahmoudAlyosify/horus-sentinel

chunks.title: RL-Cloud-Autoscaler — Deep RL for Cloud Resource Provisioning
chunks.text: RL-Cloud-Autoscaler is an autonomous cloud resource provisioning system using deep reinforcement learning, built May 2026 to June 2026. Mahmoud built a custom Gymnasium environment simulating cloud workload dynamics and trained PPO and DQN agents to make autonomous provisioning decisions in real time. He optimised the cost–latency trade-off under fluctuating demand, benchmarking both algorithms against static and reactive threshold-based autoscaling baselines. Repository: https://github.com/MahmoudAlyosify/RL-Cloud-Autoscaler

chunks.text: Dr. Rahatara Ferdousi, who taught Mahmoud Generative AI and supervises his master's research, describes him as an active, highly engaged student with constant curiosity and initiative, whose ability to connect theoretical ideas to practical implementation stood out. Dr. Ibrahim Elsemman, Associate Professor of Information Systems at Assiut University, describes him as among the best students in the Faculty of Computers and Information, innovative in his projects, and quick to absorb new technologies. Dr. Islam Taj-Eddin notes his remarkable technical knowledge and systematic approach to problem solving. Colleagues describe strong leadership, effective communication, and problem-solving that was decisive in project success.
